GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Hand-rolled port of ShrinkerBeetle.cs:31-44: SHRINKER_MOVE (initial) -> CHOMP_MOVE -> STOMP_MOVE -> CHOMP_MOVE, i.e. the debuff happens exactly once and then the two attacks alternate forever -- SHRINKER is never returned to. The port's _TRANSITIONS encodes those three edges. Executed, not asserted (verdict rule 5): `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py chain` rebuilds the C# GenerateMoveStateMachine graph node for node on the sim's OWN MonsterMoveStateMachine primitives (so the walk, the repeat rules and the single-NextFloat(total) draw are the audited machinery) and diffs it against the shipped port over 20 turns from an identically seeded RunRngSet. Result: 20/20 turns identical and 0 MonsterAi draws on both sides.

guards.what: ShrinkMove applies ShrinkPower with amount MINUS ONE (ShrinkerBeetle.cs:51, `-1m`)
guards.rationale: The sign is load-bearing and the port keeps it: `PowerCmd.apply(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, ShrinkPower, -1, applier=self)` (shrinker_beetle.py:40), and the telegraph shows Intent(DEBUFF, buffs=[(ShrinkPower, -1)]) (:31). PROMPT.md bug class 3 (sign-aware power typing) checked: the amount is negative, so any GetTypeForAmount classification of the applied power must be the debuff arm -- that is ShrinkPower's own question and belongs to the power tier, but the monster passes the right sign. The move targets `targets` (the player) on both sides, not the beetle.

guards.what: Range-bound convention on the initial-HP roll: Rng.NextInt(min, max) is max-EXCLUSIVE (Rng.cs:101-109) where Python's random.randint(a, b) INCLUDES b
guards.rationale: Checked as a convention, not just as constants. The GAME's range is [MinInitialHp, MaxInitialHp] INCLUSIVE, because Creature.SetUniqueMonsterHpValue compensates for the exclusive bound explicitly: `int num = Monster.MaxInitialHp + 1` (Creature.cs:378) feeds BOTH `Enumerable.Range(minInitialHp, num - minInitialHp)` (Creature.cs:379) and the fallback `rng.NextInt(minInitialHp, num)` (Creature.cs:383). The sim's parity port matches on both arms: `candidates = [v for v in range(lo, hi + 1) ...]` picked with `niche.next_int_range(0, len(candidates))`, fallback `niche.next_int_range(lo, hi + 1)` (combat.py:224-243), and `next_int_range` is itself max-exclusive (rng.py:182-186) -- so the two `+ 1`s land exactly where C# puts them. This unit has a real 3-wide range, so a top-end off-by-one would be silently observable as HP 40 never occurring. Executed (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py hprange`, 400 seeded combats per unit): declared [38,40], observed [38,40], and the observed set is exactly the full inclusive range, so the top endpoint 40 does occur. All 15 units of this batch pass. NOTE the legacy (non-parity) path is also right by a different route: Monster.__init__'s `rng.randint(self.min_hp, self.max_hp)` (monsters/base.py:78) is inclusive on both ends, matching the game's inclusive range, and in parity mode it is overwritten before anything reads it. Rule 7: Creature.cs, Rng.cs, sts2_rl/combat.py and sts2_rl/rng.py are hashed in extra_sources.
